report.scope: Tube-format watercolor only (no pans, gouache or acrylic), for a buyer who has bought paint before and wants the most usable paint per dollar.

primer.what_it_is: Soft, concentrated paint you squeeze onto a palette and thin with water. Tubes give far more paint per dollar than pans and suit anyone painting regularly.

must_haves.why: More pigment, less filler, so colors stay vivid and mix cleanly.

must_haves.feature: Pigment code on every tube (e.g. PB29)
must_haves.why: Shows exactly what's in the tube, so you can compare brands and avoid mystery mixes.
Rates fade resistance. Without it, paintings can fade.
They mix predictably and stay clean.
Needed to compute cost per ml, since tubes range from 5 to 37 ml.

premium_features.feature: Mineral and granulating colors (Daniel Smith PrimaTek, Genuine)
premium_features.why: Textured, unique effects; you pay for pigment rarity.
Keeps paint moist and rewets easily; the premium is small.
Brighter and more opaque than "hue" substitutes, but 30–60% more per tube.

premium_features.why: Helps if you want unusual colors; irrelevant for a limited palette.

normalization.unit: Adjusted dollars per ml of artist-grade-equivalent paint
normalization.unit_rationale: Per-tube or per-set prices mislead: a 5 ml and a 15 ml tube differ 3×, and a 12 ml student tube holds less pigment than a 12 ml artist tube. A hobbyist uses tubes down, so tube count isn't the constraint.
normalization.quality_adjustment: Quality multiplier (set by judgment, not lab tests) = pigment load × lightfast usability × (1 − waste). Artist grade (DS, M. Graham, Schmincke, Holbein, Sennelier, W&N Pro, Jackson's, Blick Artists'): 1.0. Mid-student (Cotman, Van Gogh, Rembrandt): about 0.5–0.6. Dyed or washable kids' paint (Crayola, Prang, Sargent): about 0.2. Student paint costs roughly double its sticker price per ml.

consensus.expert_view: Bruce MacEvoy (Handprint), repeated by review sites (affiliate-style, weak sources): student paints carry more dextrin filler and less pigment, dry duller and matte, and are often "hue" mixes. Jane Blundell's swatches across ~50 brands, with pigment codes, support comparing by pigment rather than brand.
consensus.community_view: r/Watercolor: above student grade the "best" brand is subjective. Sennelier is "magic" for soft transparent layers; M. Graham is "gorgeous" for smooth washes and bold pigment load. Brand name alone doesn't guarantee quality because most brands sell several lines. Old Holland is seen as the most expensive tier.
consensus.where_they_disagree: Little real conflict: experts focus on grade and pigment data, while the community says brand choice above student grade is a matter of taste. Wet Canvas, Handprint and Doodlewash pages were not scanned directly.
